name: Toyota GR86
reliability: 8/10 — simple, light, naturally aspirated; few chronic issues
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate-High (sports coupe, but cheap & low-power) · Maintenance ~$755/yr
popular_mods: Forced induction (HKS turbo / supercharger kits, 300+ hp) — main power path
Cold air intake, catback exhaust, Tomei header
ECU tune (modest NA gains — power isn't this car's strength)
Coilovers, sway bars, chassis bracing, sticky tires — transforms the car
Big brake kit for track use

generations.1st Gen ZN6 — Scion FR-S (2012–2016): 200hp 2.0L FA20 flat-4. Co-developed with Subaru (sold as BRZ). Scion branding in the US until the brand was killed in 2016.
generations.1st Gen ZN6 — Toyota 86 (2017–2020): 205hp after revised gear ratios and minor tune update. Rebranded Toyota 86 after Scion was discontinued.
generations.2nd Gen ZN8 — Toyota GR86 (2022–present): 228hp 2.4L FA24 — 18% more power, 11% more torque. Subaru Global Platform adds 50% more torsional rigidity. Nearly a full second quicker to 60.

common_issues: Low torque at low RPM — power lives above 4,500 rpm (1st gen especially)
Clutch wear if slipping on spirited launches
maintenance_tips: Let revs climb before shifting — engine rewards high RPM
Brake fluid degrades quickly on track — flush every season
Tires wear fast under spirited driving — check pressure often

engine.detail: Naturally aspirated 2.4L FA24 Subaru flat-four, 228 hp / 184 lb-ft, that loves to rev past 7,000 rpm with the power living up top.
engine.watch: The real risk is track oil starvation - sustained right-hand lateral g can drop oil pressure and spin a rod bearing; early cars also had RTV sealant clogging the oil pickup.

drivetrain.detail: RWD through a slick Aisin 6-speed manual (or 6-speed auto), with a Torsen limited-slip diff standard.
drivetrain.watch: The gearbox and diff are tough; the clutch is the wear item - riding or slipping it on hard launches burns it early.

suspension.detail: MacPherson struts up front, double wishbones out back on Subaru's Global Platform - about 50% stiffer than the first-gen chassis.
suspension.watch: No chronic faults; it's just soft and tail-happy stock - sway bars, coilovers, and sticky tires wake it right up.

brakes.detail: Ventilated discs at all four corners - plenty for the street on a ~2,800-lb car.
brakes.watch: Stock pads and fluid fade fast on track; flush the fluid every season and fit track pads before lapping hard.

fuel.detail: D-4S dual injection runs both direct and port injectors on the FA24.
fuel.watch: That dual setup sidesteps the intake-valve carbon buildup that plagues direct-injection-only engines - basically trouble-free.
